messages:
sam: FYI I'm kicking off a retrocompute for Q1 aggregates to fix missing hourly totals for several tenants. expecting ~18h of work if run at current concurrency.
anjali: :eyes: which queue are you planning to use? reserved or the normal backfill pool?
mike: if it hits the normal pool it will stomp on production requests. we should gate it behind a priority tag and smaller windows.
sam: agreed. plan was normal pool but with a soft throttle. thinking tag:priority=high-retrocompute and a 10% concurrency cap across tenants.
tess: can we instead use a preemptible lane that can be evicted on latency spikes? that way we don't need to touch prod quotas.
mike: +1 for preemptible. allocator already has preemptible slots for model training. we can reuse that concept for backfills but need tenant isolation.
kai: two implementation asks: 1) metadata label on the job so routing knows to put it in preemptible pool, 2) Console should show a banner and ability to mark a job "allow-preempt".
sam: for (1) i'll add job.metadata.priority=retro-high and job.metadata.preemptible=true in the submit payload.
anjali: how will fair-share work? if one tenant floods with retro jobs they should be limited.
mike: allocator change: treat preemptible backfill slots as separate resource pool with per-tenant weights. algorithm: round-robin by weight, but stop after X tokens/sec change on prod.
tess: UX: console needs a live card that lists "Active Retrocomputes" with tenant, start time, progress, and an emergency pause button.
kai: also add an opt-out flag per-tenant for privacy/regulatory customers so we don't automatically put their job into shared preemptible lanes.
backfill-bot: retrocompute job 4825550000-qt1 queued (id=rt-2026-04-12-7). priority=retro-high, preemptible=true
mike: cost estimate note: preemptible lanes can run cheaper but more retries will increase total. put a budget cap on the job submission (job.max_cost=1500USD).
sam: adding job.max_cost now. also adding a canary: run 1 shard first, wait 30m and validate dashboard consistency before full run.
anjali: good. make sure telemetry-alerting has a canary filter so we don't alert on expected in-flight deltas. add tag canary:true.
kai: routing change will be small: check label "preemptible=true" then assign to pool "backfill-preemptible". I'll open a PR and link a quick patch to the allocator config.
tess: on the console side i'll wire up an action that POSTs to /internal/backfills/{id}/pause and a small toast when paused. should we require SSO admin for pause?
sam: yes require admin for pause. normal engineers can propose but admins confirm.
mike: one more thought: lets surface an estimated ETA and token usage in the job submit modal. makes it easier to reason about cost vs urgency.
anjali: agree. for dataset/tenant-scoped throttles: add a per-tenant cap field in the submit form (default 5% of tenant production qps).
backfill-bot: rt-2026-04-12-7-canary started on shard 1 at 4825550060. status=running
sam: canary logs looked good so far, no spike in production latencies. continuing to ramp.
mike: after canary, we should enqueue remaining shards in small windows (30m windows, 10 shards each) to reduce load variance.
anjali: schedule approved. who owns the follow-up to add console banner + admin pause? @tess
tess: I'll take it, will open a small RFC and a patch by EOD.
kai: i'll open allocator PR and add unit tests for pool selection by metadata label. linking both PRs in the thread when ready.
sam: thanks everyone. tagging next steps: sam (monitor & validate), mike (cost cap guardrails), anjali (throttle defaults), tess (console UX+pause), kai (allocator routing). will post updates here.
backfill-bot: rt-2026-04-12-7 progress=1/120 shards completed. next window scheduled in 20m.
